(a) 
Section 9 of the Act of September 6, 1958 (7 U.S.C. 1431b), is amended, effective January 1, 1967, by deleting the symbol “(1)”, by changing the semicolon to a period and by striking out all of the language in the section after the semicolon.
 
    (b) Section 709 of the Food and Agriculture Act of 1965 (7 U.S.C. 1446a–1) is amended, effective January 1, 1967, by striking out “foreign distribution,”.
 
    (c) Section 416 of the Agricultural Act of 1949, as amended (7 U.S.C. 1431), is amended, effective January 1, 1967, by striking out the following: “and (4) to donate any such food commodities in excess of anticipated disposition under (1), (2), and (3) above to nonprofit voluntary agencies registered with the Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid of the Foreign Operations Administration or other appropriate department or agency of the Federal Government and intergovernmental organizations for use in the assistance of needy persons and in nonprofit school lunch programs outside the United States”; “and (4) above”; “, in the case of commodities made available for use within the United States, or their delivery free alongside ship or free on board export carrier at point of export, in the case of commodities made available for use outside the United States”; and “The assistance to needy persons provided in (4) above shall, insofar as practicable be directed toward community and other self-help designed to alleviate the causes of the need for such assistance.”
 
    (d) Section 8 of Public Law 85–931 (72 Stat. 1792) is amended (1) by inserting a period in lieu of the colon after the word “Act” and striking out the proviso; (2) by inserting after the word “manufactured” the word “entirely”; and (3) by inserting before the comma following the words “surplus supply” the words “in the same manner as any other agricultural commodity or product is made available”.
 
    (e) Section 407 of the Agricultural Act of 1949, as amended, is amended by striking the period at the end of the third sentence thereof and adding the following: “: 
Provided, That whenever the Secretary of Agriculture determines that the carryover at the end of any marketing year of a price supported agricultural commodity for which a voluntary adjustment program is in effect will be less than 25 per centum (35 per centum in the case of wheat) of the estimated export and domestic consumption of such commodity during such marketing year, the Commodity Credit Corporation shall not sell any of its stocks of such commodity during such year for unrestricted use at less than 115 per centum (120 per centum in the case of wheat whenever its carry-over will be less than 25 per centum of such estimated export and domestic consumption) of the current price support loan plus reasonable carrying charges.”

fable.w: The section makes technical amendments to agricultural statutes and adds a pricing floor on Commodity Credit Corporation sales that is triggered by a unilateral determination of the Secretary of Agriculture. The tempting reading is the mention of "nonprofit voluntary agencies" and "intergovernmental organizations", but that language is being struck and described them only as recipients of donated commodities, not as parties consulted on a federal decision. Nothing provides for a hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, outside consultation, or a right to sue.
fable.s: whenever the Secretary of Agriculture determines that the carryover at the end of any marketing year of a price supported agricultural commodity

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to existing statutes, primarily striking out text or modifying internal administrative procedures. Subsection (c) removes language regarding donations to nonprofit agencies, but does not create a new requirement for consultation or participation with those agencies. Subsection (e) involves a determination by the Secretary of Agriculture and the Commodity Credit Corporation, which are federal entities, without any mandated input from outside parties. No public comment periods, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultations with states/tribes are established.
qwen_block.s: Section 416 of the Agricultural Act of 1949, as amended (7 U.S.C. 1431), is amended, effective January 1, 1967, by striking out the following: “and (4) to donate any such food commodities in excess of anticipated disposition under (1), (2), and (3) above to nonprofit voluntary agencies registered with the Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid of the Foreign Operations Administration or other appropriate department or agency of the Federal Government and intergovernmental organizations for use in the assistance of needy persons and in nonprofit school lunch programs outside the United States”
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "nonprofit voluntary agencies" or "intergovernmental organizations" in subsection (c) implies participation. However, this subsection is an amendment that *strikes out* language regarding donations to these entities. It does not establish a new process for consultation, coordination, or public input; it merely removes a previous provision. Furthermore, the other subsections involve internal administrative changes or reports to Congress (which is inside the government). There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with outsiders before making a decision.

opus.w: The section only makes technical amendments to commodity-disposal laws and sets a resale price limit for Commodity Credit Corporation stocks that applies when the Secretary of Agriculture makes a determination alone. The mention of nonprofit voluntary agencies is language being struck out, and even before that those agencies only received donations; they had no role in any federal decision. No consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking authority, advisory body or right to sue is created.
opus.s: to donate any such food commodities in excess of anticipated disposition under (1), (2), and (3) above to nonprofit voluntary agencies registered with the Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** The tempting reading is that the section involves outsiders, because the struck text in (c) mentions "nonprofit voluntary agencies" and "intergovernmental organizations." That reading fails for two reasons. First, the language is being deleted. Second, those groups only received donated food. They never took part in a federal decision. The rest of the section is technical amendments plus a resale price limit for Commodity Credit Corporation stocks, which applies when the Secretary of Agriculture makes a determination alone. Nothing in it calls for consultation, hearings, rulemaking, advisory bodies or a right to sue.

2. **Answer.**

qwen_chat.w: This section amends statutes regarding the donation of agricultural commodities. While it mentions nonprofit agencies and intergovernmental organizations, it does so to define recipients of donations, not to establish a participatory role in federal decision-making. There is no requirement for consultation, comment periods, or advisory roles for outside parties in the decision-making process described.
qwen_chat.s: and (4) to donate any such food commodities in excess of anticipated disposition under (1), (2), and (3) above to nonprofit voluntary agencies registered with the Committee on Voluntary Foreign Aid of the Foreign Operations Administration or other appropriate department or agency of the Federal Government and intergovernmental organizations for use in the assistance of needy persons and in nonprofit school lunch programs outside the United States
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "nonprofit voluntary agencies" and "intergovernmental organizations".
Resolution: The text describes amendments to existing laws regarding the donation of food commodities. It does not establish a process for these outside entities to consult with or participate in federal decision-making; rather, it defines the scope of donations. The mention of these entities is in the context of who receives donations, not who helps make decisions.
